closedOrMerged.title: RR-20: improve PowerPoint layout defaults and source recovery
closedOrMerged.body:
Export the coordinated array-area layouts and editorial defaults to PowerPoint, including neutral structural rules, aligned numeric cells, compact metric/quote positioning and timelines. Native magnitude axes include zero while authored overrides remain respected.

Unchanged imports recover authored rich-text style presence and adapted single-column chart source data only while provenance matches. Native list-description edits now retain source identity so the edited text style can be recovered. Repository-native test actions support bounded text-style edits and optional font-descriptor capture.

The font-observation worker now retains its failure latch when any of the seven descriptor-chain property getters throws. Explicit adapted getter reads preserve legitimate missing and mixed values and prevent later reads after failure. The source fix is `4f8a3551060d350d059ac4fdd29257c6d234fa12`.

Validation: the list-identity runtime previously passed all 138 package test files with unchanged strict archive expectations. Bounded style-action controls passed six accepted and 23 rejected plans on Windows without Office. Portable PowerShell 7.6.7 reproduced the getter failure before the fix; the corrected harness passes all 15 font controls, and managed/script getter probes verify strict latching plus normal, missing and null values. Syntax, source-policy, runner and fragment checks pass. The existing Windows test lane now includes a bounded non-Office COM-adapter probe; Windows PowerShell 5.1, actual PowerPoint descriptor capture and native acceptance remain pending. Earlier metrics lifecycle and 13-shape geometry observations do not establish full native fidelity.

closedOrMerged.body:
Array-based layout areas work throughout composition, layout selection, code editing and playground examples. Legacy space-separated rows are rejected consistently with core; content, selection, edits and undo remain preserved.

Validation: all 72 source test files pass. Prior candidate qualification covers 21 playground suites, 11 registered browser suites and six-package installed consumer checks. The shared installed timeline workflow now passes all 16 editing/export cases with two strict overflow controls against this unchanged editor runtime. These results are source/candidate qualification, not published-package or native PowerPoint acceptance.
